selected_experiment.question: Among new substitution-argument identities for already-seen expressions, do the arguments fall into a small stable consequential family shared by both deep-list cases?
selected_experiment.argument_family_signature: root tag; for applications, application-spine head kind/name plus arity and immediate argument tags; for binders/let/proj, shallow immediate child tags only

classification_rule.small_stable_family: same dominant family in both cases, <= 16 sampled families, top-8 coverage >= 0.95 in each, and dominant family count >= 50000 in each
classification_rule.stable_heavy_tail: same dominant family in both cases and top-8 coverage >= 0.70 in each, but small_stable_family is false

post_result_policy.if_small_stable_family: compile argument-family quotient separator and prospectively inspect exact consequence preservation inside the dominant family before any cross-argument reuse
post_result_policy.if_stable_heavy_tail: split dominant substitution-argument family from tail and reclose before a narrower quotient experiment
post_result_policy.if_distributed_arguments: compile obstruction against a compact argument-family quotient and move to argument-generation provenance

claim_boundary: Diagnostic family counting only. Distinct substitution arguments remain semantically distinct; no cross-argument cache reuse or substitution quotient is authorized.
